query:
All highly successful salespersons are both well organized and self-motivated, characteristics absent from many salespersons who are not highly successful. Further, although only those who are highly successful are well known among their peers, no salespersons who are self-motivated regret their career choices.

If all of the statements above are true, no salespersons who are well known among their peers regret their career choices must be true.

repl_history.response:
Let's examine the preview.

After reviewing the passage in the [Global Context Preview], I notice that although only those who are highly successful are well known among their peers, no salespersons who regret their career choices directly correlates with them not being self-motivated or well-organized which is true for "many" non-highly successful sales persons. Moreover: 'no salespersons who ARE self-motivated regret their careers'. Thus, combining this it shows there can't be a person who regrets and is well known (among peers) by implication - so they must not HAVE to know each other if no one who regrets fits either category.

FINAL ANSWER: entailment
